items.title: Mark Soskin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 17, 2021
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I’ve noticed that a lot, not a lot, but frequently with for instance Miles Davis... [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah well try to do it.

ctx.x: Because you have to make it right. You have to make the wrong note sound right. You have to convince the person or people that this is the right thing to play. You know it works on this chord. You know? And I’ll have to do that tonight. I’ll have to make it work.

I’ve noticed that a lot, not a lot, but frequently with for instance Miles Davis, that he’ll play, especially like at the ends of phrases he’ll choose a note or play a note that boy I wish I could think of something like that, but I’m not sure I would dare play it.

Yeah well try to do it. Find out. You know I mean if you want to create music it’s taking risks. And that risk taking is often what makes the thing happen. You know just throwing caution to the wind, again.
